title: Commercial backflow inspection: scope the asset before you book
description: A decision page for facilities teams to identify the assembly, service scope, access needs, and reporting owner before a commercial backflow inspection.
prompt: What exact commercial deliverable is needed: condition visit, certified test, repair scope, or filed report?
answer: Commercial inspection becomes useful only when the asset, access conditions, tester requirement, service limits, and report owner are written into the work order. Inspection and compliance filing are different deliverables.
urgency: Escalate a mismatched asset record, inaccessible assembly, active leakage, or deadline before authorizing a generic visit.
diagramAlt: Backflow test workflow from assembly identification through report receipt

choices.label: I have a notice or compliance deadline
choices.detail: Use the notice?셲 account, assembly, due date, and submission instructions as the source of truth.

choices.label: I need a condition or maintenance visit
choices.detail: Ask whether the visit includes a certified test, repair authorization, and utility filing.

choices.label: I manage several properties
choices.detail: Build one asset list with address, location, assembly type, serial number, last test, and reporting owner.

steps.title: Establish the governing record
steps.body: Build a site packet with notice, last report, contacts, photos, and access constraints.

steps.title: Define the complete work
steps.body: Ask the provider to state whether inspection, certified test, repair, retest, and filing are included.

steps.title: Document completion
steps.body: Attach completed results and proof of filing to the right asset record.

safeChecks: Use the exact property and assembly record before authorizing work.
Confirm official program and manufacturer information for the decision.
Keep the final result and submission evidence together.
stopConditions: The scope does not name the assembly or responsible party.
The proposal treats an inspection as proof of compliance.
identifiers: A portfolio record should include asset tag, model, size, location, and last result.
Tenant access and mechanical-room rules change the real visit scope.
A report must be matched to the correct property and assembly.
notThisDevice: A generic online part or device listing does not establish the correct field scope.
A different water-system use can require a different approval and service workflow.
This planning page does not replace a qualified on-site assessment.
evidenceNote: This path is governed by the official utility or authority requirement, then by exact manufacturer documentation for the identified assembly.
